thesis: Intel priced an upsized $20B equity offering at $95/share on 2026-08-12; the stock has since traded down to $87.26, leaving those buyers roughly $1.5B under water, and the 60-day close-to-close move is -32.2% (132.87 -> 90.07). The disclosed raise sits on top of reported CPU share at a three-decade low and heavy capex, so the drawdown reflects a company-disclosed dilution and execution problem rather than only the broader semiconductor de-rating that also hit the group on 2026-08-24. The counter-case is that the raise funds the foundry build-out and the stock is 38% off its high, which some read as the risk already priced; that does not resolve the read here, because the offering is a confirmed increase in share count against a shrinking core franchise, not a one-off. This suggests supply and share-loss pressure persists near term.
invalidation: Intel discloses foundry customer wins or CPU share stabilization that reverses the market-share trend, or the stock reclaims the $95 offering price on sustained volume
sources: Law360 (Supreme Court October argument, Intel 401(k) suit): https://www.law360.com/securities/articles/2509623

thesis: Marvell's 60-day close-to-close move is -15.7% (281.26 -> 237.04), but the sourced explanation is sector and macro rather than company-specific: the semiconductor group sold off with SOXX down 3%, rising Treasury yields pressured high-multiple chip names, and holders trimmed a stock still up roughly 179% year to date. No company disclosure accounts for the decline. Fiscal results are scheduled for 2026-08-27, three days out, which leaves the read unresolved in both directions. This suggests the drawdown is positioning-driven ahead of an unresolved binary event rather than evidence of disclosed deterioration.
invalidation: the 2026-08-27 earnings report shows AI networking revenue or guidance below consensus, confirming a fundamental rather than positioning-driven decline

thesis: Alliance Laundry traded 3.00x its 30-day average volume on 2026-08-24 with the 60-day close-to-close move at -11.0% (26.37 -> 23.47). The sourced cause is a disclosed secondary: principal stockholder BDT Capital Partners priced an upsized offering of 22,550,000 shares at $23.50, and the stock is now pinned near that price. Operationally the company reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-11 with net revenue $477M (+7% y/y), gross margin 39.8% (+90bp), adjusted EBITDA $134M (+12%) and adjusted EPS $0.41 against a $0.35 consensus, and raised the low end of full-year guidance. The counter-case is that a large insider sale can signal the sponsor's own view of value; that is not resolved here, and the supply overhang is a real near-term weight. This suggests the price weakness is largely mechanical secondary supply against improving disclosed operating results, an offsetting rather than a clear net read.
invalidation: Q3 revenue growth or adjusted EBITDA margin falls below the raised full-year guidance range, or the stock breaks and holds below the $23.50 offering price
sources: StockTitan (EY ratified as 2026 auditor, no restatement): https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/ALH/8-k-alliance-laundry-holdings-inc-reports-material-event-6b4ae2ec8b06.html

thesis: Apple's 60-day close-to-close move is +12.4% (275.15 -> 309.35) on already-reported, company-disclosed results rather than anticipation: fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $109.42B (+16.4% y/y), iPhone $54.25B, and Services at a record $30.74B, the third consecutive quarter of roughly 16% revenue growth, with China iPhone sales running 23% higher. The strongest counter-evidence is regulatory: on 2026-07-08 the EU General Court dismissed all three of Apple's gatekeeper challenges, locking in DMA App Store and iOS obligations that bear directly on Services economics. That does not change the read, because the record Services quarter was reported under that same compliance regime rather than before it, so the disclosed revenue trend already absorbs the ruling. The separate DOJ case is in early settlement talks with no scheduled trial date. This suggests the move reflects a confirmed and broad-based revenue reacceleration; the anticipated September foldable is not part of this read.
invalidation: fiscal Q4 revenue growth decelerates materially below the roughly 16% run rate, Services growth stalls, or the DOJ case moves to a scheduled trial with structural App Store remedies on the table

thesis: AMD's 60-day close-to-close move is -11.1% (532.57 -> 473.25). One specific, confirmed company event sits inside that: SpaceX said it will build its computing infrastructure exclusively on Nvidia silicon, with Elon Musk calling Vera Rubin the best architecture, and AMD fell 8.8% to $473 on that news. Against it, AMD guided third-quarter revenue to about $13B plus or minus $300M, above the roughly $12.52B consensus. The remainder of the drawdown is attributed to sector profit-taking, rising Treasury yields and high-beta positioning ahead of Nvidia's report rather than to AMD disclosures. The evidence is therefore offsetting — a marquee AI customer lost to the direct competitor against guidance that still runs ahead of consensus — and this run does not resolve which dominates.
invalidation: AMD discloses a comparable-scale AI accelerator design win that offsets the SpaceX loss, or third-quarter revenue lands below the roughly $12.7B low end of its own guidance

thesis: SpaceX's 60-day close-to-close move is -10.5% (153.00 -> 136.97), and the stock fell below its IPO price around 2026-08-20. The disclosed driver is the Q2 2026 report on 2026-08-04: results topped Wall Street expectations, but capital expenditure rose more than sixfold year over year to $18.37B, of which $15.83B went to AI infrastructure, and shares fell 6% after hours. The counter-evidence is operational and real — Starlink reached 12 million subscribers, double a year earlier, and the AI segment is growing on cloud agreements, Grok and X subscriptions and government contracts. That does not resolve the read, because the market is repricing near-term free cash flow against that growth and the spending path has not been bounded by guidance. A separate FAA-led mishap investigation gates Starship launch resumption but carries no scheduled ruling date. This suggests an unresolved spending-versus-growth trade rather than a clear net read.
invalidation: SpaceX guides capital expenditure down or frames a peak-spend quarter, or Starlink subscriber growth decelerates while capex stays at the Q2 run rate
